title: Microsoft 365 admin center: migrate Google Groups to Microsoft 365 Groups
summary: Hold: the Graph membership guidance presents a delegated-access role requirement as applying to every call, although application permissions are also supported. The page also asserts that existing controls do not govern the migration service when their applicability is unknown. Roadmap facts and the documented control paths and endpoints otherwise check out.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Owners and members can be reviewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Teams & groups > Active teams & groups > group > Membership.
claims.quote: Expand Teams & groups, and then click Active teams & groups. Click the name of the group ... On the Membership tab, choose if you want to manage Owners or Members. Choose Add ... or click X to remove someone.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which reaches the right tab, and add to controls[2].note: 'On Membership, choose Owners or Members; choose Add to add someone or X to remove someone.' This completes the route documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/create-groups/manage-groups without changing the row's scope.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref adds group members, not owners.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref ... supply a JSON object that contains an @odata.id property with a reference by ID to a supported group member object type.
claims.fix: Keep controls[2].api.call unchanged and add to its note: 'The request body sets @odata.id to a reference to the user being added.' The pre-check's missing-endpoint warning is a false positive: the endpoint appears in Example 1 at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/group-post-members?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: The cited Entra UI instructions require at least Global Administrator for the group-creation setting.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Changing membership through the Graph call requires a supported Microsoft Entra role, such as Groups Administrator, or group ownership.
claims.quote: In delegated scenarios, the signed-in user must also be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role ... Group owners ... Groups Administrator. Supported resource: user; Application: GroupMember.ReadWrite.All.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'In delegated scenarios, the signed-in user adding members through Graph must also have a supported Microsoft Entra role, such as Groups Administrator, or be a group owner.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/group-post-members?view=graph-rest-1.0. The reference also supports application access, so do not state the signed-in-user requirement for every call.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 group controls allow administrators to review and change destination-group owners and members.

claims.claim: The existing group-control rows do not govern the migration service itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Google Groups" migration service enable administrator permissions default; "Google Groups" migration Microsoft Graph beta PowerShell API. claims.fix: Replace 'they do not govern the migration service itself' with 'the membership controls govern destination groups; whether the group-creation restriction applies to the migration service is not yet documented'.
